title: Zutty Singleton and Paul Barbarin, and being fired from a show band
summary: Foster tells how Zutty replaced Barbarin in a band, and Zutty's too-fast tempos.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's what Dixon was on. Yeah, that's a short sound job. And I'll tell you, I'm going to tell you the reason that, Manuel, and you know it. Our drummers would play it in our jazz band, in our rag-tonged band those days. They tuned, they know how to tune those snares. See, you got to tune those snares. The snares got to be gauged, just like the strings on a violin, on a bass violin. They got to be tuned, and you got a row of snares on them things, and the snares all got to be correct, not too loose, they all got to be perfect. See? Because you got them things to tune those snares. See, when they buy the things, they type them, and the things are so tight, the drums sound like, just like this, just like this wood you hit, that's what you see. They don't know, and you can't tell them nothing. And I haven't called this guy a name. I could call his name. Well, I'm sorry, you don't have to. Yeah, I'm going to call his name. Yeah, I'm going to call his name. Lou Leslie wanted to, Lou Leslie was a black boy, hired Zutty Singleton, to play drums for the big show down there, see. Had the music and all, see drums in the big shows. In the big shows they had out east and out west, big shows. The main thing was your trumpet and your trombone and your drums. See? Because you had to have that strong lead and that drums, with catching those guys when they danced. Zutty would catch it after the man and kick it and go and sit down and Zutty would come out with the cymbal. And he'd say, boom, see. Then when the man got after him he said he played with Lou Armstrong. I said I'm sitting in the audience, listening to this rehearsal. We used to have a boy boy sitting in the North Carolina. We would go to the rehearsal, we'd go down and catch them chorus girls and we'd be able to check on that. And wait until she finished rehearsal so we could go down and have a little fun. We'd have a lot of spots, we'd have just like the alley, you know. We'd have a little bit of a ball. So he had a guy, I forget his name, he's dead, and I hit really big ears. He played tenters and everything else. I said there's a drummer back there. So that's how Zutty didn't make those things. See? And Zutty, they was going to fire Paul Bobbins out of King Arnold's band for Zutty. Well they were hoisting Zutty on the slide, all north of Paul, for his show. Well Paul could read. You've got to read them drums apart. And Paul and Louis Russell, see all his western years, they might not get played on a whole lot but all of them can read music. That's right. See? But Louis Russell had taught Paul a whole lot of music while he was up there at Woodwood King, Orlando Plantation, Chicago. So he'll come down and play the show, and who they're going to play? Barney, Bigall, Nick. Nick, I think. I think they had Donnell Howell in the band too with him. Yeah, I think they had Donnell Howell in the band. George F. was the next man. Well all the Reeds got together, and they fired Paul, they fired him.

Fireed him in the liquor. Well, see Paul was a downtown boy, Zutty a downtown boy. He ain't got no voice, you know what I mean? See? Well he couldn't make it, see? And I had him, I got him his first job with the tuxedo. He was a great talker, and you had to play it to his rhythm. Don't care how fast you knock off a band, you had to come down to him, see? And that's why he, and he was one of those bigger guys who always wanted to fight.
I know he messed up the Ori band sometimes on the broadcast, playing things too fast, like Muscat Ramble. Ori couldn't even play it that fast.

Well, Zutty couldn't play it that fast. So Muscat Ramble is not a slow number the way Ori played. See? See the older them guys get, they don't try to elevate, they stay the same stage, just like Rangie was telling you last night. You don't play like they played years ago, because it's different. See?
